document.description: On Unix, Alacritty's IPC listener decodes JSON CreateWindow, Config, and GetConfig messages and posts them into the GUI event loop. These controls are distinct from terminal-program OSC 52 clipboard requests: the terminal core defaults to OnlyCopy, accepting clipboard writes but rejecting reads. Scrollback configuration separately caps retained history at 100,000 lines at this revision.
document.name: IPC, configuration, and process resource boundary

document.description: Consul maintains a catalog of services and nodes and exposes queries for discovering registered service instances. Registration and lookup are separate from the application protocol carried by those services.
document.name: Catalog-backed service discovery

document.description: Docker images are composed from immutable layers and containers add a writable layer, allowing shared image content with per-container changes.
document.name: Content-addressed image and filesystem layers

document.description: Dovecot uses separate login services for protocols such as IMAP, POP3, ManageSieve, and submission. Login processes run in restricted environments, can be bounded by service process and client limits, and transfer an authenticated connection to a post-login mail process; this implementation boundary is distinct from the IMAP or POP3 protocol specifications.
document.name: Protocol-specific login isolation and session limits

document.description: Blobs, trees, commits, and annotated tags are addressed by identifiers derived from their serialized content.
document.name: Content-addressed object storage

document.description: Branches and tags provide names that point to objects while the referenced objects remain immutable.
document.name: Mutable reference layer

document.description: libuv separates long-lived handles from short-lived requests. Initialized handles are closed asynchronously and their memory may be reclaimed after the close callback; requests carry operation context until completion or cancellation, with operation-specific cleanup where documented.
document.name: Handle and request lifecycle

document.description: Tab stores current directory/file, history, cursor pointer, path, and ancestor pathway. Movement and tab-change signals update the active file and restore the tab's saved pointer into the directory object. Selection returns marked entries when present and otherwise the current file.
document.name: Tab-local navigation state over directory objects

document.description: What does the loader's work budget constrain, and where can a job exceed it?
document.name: Cooperative work-queue transition system

document.description: In WAL mode, committed changes are appended to a separate log and readers use an end mark to observe a stable database snapshot while a writer appends. Checkpointing later transfers WAL content back into the main database file.
document.name: Write-ahead logging with reader snapshots

document.description: Patterns and contextual selectors are compiled against language-specific syntax kinds, while parser construction rejects incompatible Tree-sitter languages and configuration rejects unknown top-level keys. Consequently grammar, matcher, and rule-schema changes can affect existing rule behavior even when the source snippet still looks similar. The workspace version and dependency requirements pin this observation to one snapshot; they do not establish compatibility across releases.
document.name: Grammar and rule compatibility boundary

document.name: Merkle-style content-addressed graph

document.description: The official architecture description separates readers that parse formats into a native document AST from writers that emit target formats. document.name: Shared document intermediate representation

document.description: Redis supports no persistence, point-in-time RDB snapshots, append-only AOF logging, or a combination. AOF recovery reconstructs the dataset by replaying write operations, while RDB provides compact snapshots.

document.description: How can Redis construct a new snapshot or rewritten log concurrently and make it the active durable representation only after completion?

document.description: How can rule and balancer updates become visible to route selection while existing selections remain valid?

document.description: StrDoc owns source text, a language value, and a Tree-sitter tree. Its edit path updates source content and tree coordinates, then reparses using the edited old tree. Tree nodes expose ranges and borrowed source text. try_new returns parsing errors while the convenience new constructor expects success; do_edit mutates content and coordinates before reparsing and can return an error, so successful reparse is a necessary condition for a coherent post-edit tree.
document.name: Coupled source, language, and syntax-tree state

document.description: didOpen transfers content management to the client, so the server must not read that open document through its URI. Open and close notifications are balanced with at most one active open per document. didChange supplies the version after its changes and either full text or ordered range edits; both notifications and edits within one notification must be applied in received order. didClose returns the master content to the URI-backed location. Clients must synchronize content before requesting information about it.
document.name: Client-owned versioned document mirrors

document.description: initialize is the first client request and may be sent only once; ordinary traffic is gated on its response, with enumerated initialization-time exceptions. initialized marks client readiness for server capability registration. shutdown requests termination of service without immediate process exit so its response can be delivered; exit subsequently asks the process to terminate. Requests after shutdown should receive InvalidRequest, and exit distinguishes prior orderly shutdown through its recommended exit code.
document.name: Initialization and two-step shutdown lifecycle

document.description: Clients opt into partial results for a supported request by providing partialResultToken. The server then reports the entire result as appending $/progress notifications and leaves the final response empty of result values. Partial results after RequestCancelled may be used if their incompleteness is made clear; after other errors they should be discarded. Work-done progress and partial-result progress have separate tokens and purposes.
document.name: Tokenized progress and incremental result delivery

document.description: Which messages are admissible given lifecycle phase, document state, and pending request IDs?
document.name: Product state machine for session phase, document ownership, and outstanding requests

document.description: Angular components pair metadata and templates with a compiled render representation, turning declarative template bindings into view instructions executed by the runtime.
document.name: Compiled component template view

document.description: Patterns are parsed into syntax-based PatternNodes with metavariables; a contextual pattern selects a node kind from a surrounding snippet. Matchers carry a capture environment and may prefilter node kinds. Pattern matching commits environment changes only on success; All commits after every operand succeeds, Any retries alternatives from the original environment and commits the first success, and Not probes with a throwaway environment. Declarative rules include atomic, relational, and composite forms.
document.name: Capture-aware syntax patterns and rule composition

document.description: The workspace separates core matching, language support, rule configuration, and CLI crates. The core Tree-sitter adapter supplies parsed documents and nodes; configuration compiles declarative rules into matchers and fixers. CLI scan selects rules for each language and path, runs CombinedScan, and delegates diagnostics or diffs to printer processors. Tree-sitter use is directly evidenced by imports, parser calls, and the workspace dependency, not inferred from architectural resemblance.
document.name: Parser, matcher, rule, and CLI component separation

document.description: The BusyBox source tree uses configuration and generated applet tables to select which applets are built into a particular binary, so the deployed command set is a build-time subset rather than a fixed universal executable.
document.name: Configuration-selected applet set

document.description: A project-oriented transformation engine that compiles declarative SQL resources into a dependency-ordered warehouse build graph with adapter-specific materializations and tests.

document.description: After scanning, the fixed bundler invokes a linker over reachable files and entry points. The linker is the boundary where module relationships, code splitting, and output serialization are turned into generated files, while the API exposes bundling and transformation as distinct operations.
document.name: Linker and output boundary

document.description: CockroachDB translates SQL requests into key-value operations, distributes the keyspace into contiguous ranges, and presents replicated ranges as a single distributed SQL database.
document.name: Layered SQL to range execution

document.description: SQLite compiles SQL text into bytecode stored in a prepared statement and executes that program with a virtual machine. Tokenization, parsing, code generation, and bytecode execution are distinct stages.
document.name: SQL compilation to bytecode and virtual-machine execution

document.description: Terraform translates configuration into resource nodes and dependency edges, using references and explicit dependencies to determine an order for planning and applying changes.
document.name: Declarative resource dependency graph

document.description: Electron exposes utilityProcess for starting Node.js environments in separate child processes and communicating with them through MessagePorts.
